30.subject: Botany
30.text: The branched sclereids present in hydrophytes
30.sol: Sclereids are highly thickened dead sclerenchyma cells with very narrow cavities. They may also be branched. They provide stiffness to the parts in which they occur. Sclereids are of many types: brachysclereids, macrosclereids, osteosclereids, astrosclereids, trichosclereids and filiform sclereids. Astrosclereids are star-shaped, having various branches or arms. They are found in intercellular spaces of leaves and stems of many hydrophytes like Nymphaea.

301.subject: Botany
301.text:
Assertion : Gibberellic acid increases length of grape stalks.
Reason : Ethophon hastens fruit ripening in tomato and apple.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
301.sol: Gibberellin increases the number and size of several fruits, e.g., grape, tomato. The hormone creates more room by increasing the size of stalks so that the fruit can grow in size. Ethophon is 2-chloroethyl phosphonic acid. In aqueous solution, ethophon slowly releases ethylene and is transported to various parts. It aids in fruit ripening in some fleshy fruits like banana, tomato, apple, mango, etc.

n Subshell
1 s
2 s, p
3 s, p,d
4 s, p, d, f

Azimuthal quantum number $( l )$:-

It describes the shape of electron cloud and number of subshell in a shell.

l Subshell
0 s
1 p
2 d
3 f

So, for $n = 3, l = 2$, this represents the $3d$ subshell. It can have the maximum ten electrons.

Hence, a subshell $n = 3, l = 2$ can accommodate maximum of $10electrons$.

6098.text: If the height of a cone of greatest volume that can be inscribed in a sphere of radius $\mathrm{R}$ is $\mathrm{kR}$, then ratio of the volume of the cone to the volume of the sphere is
6098.sol:
$\begin{aligned} & \text{ In } \triangle O D C \text{, } \\ & r^2=R^2-(h-R)^2 \\ & =2 h R-h^2\end{aligned}$
Hence volume of cone $A B C=\frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h$ $\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}=\frac{1}{3} \pi\left(2 h R-h^2\right) h=\frac{1}{3} \pi\left(2 R h^2-h^3\right)$
Now for volume to be maximum, $$ \begin{aligned} & \frac{d V}{d h}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{3 \pi}\left[4 h R-3 h^2\right]=0 \\ & \Rightarrow h \neq 0 \text{ Hence } h=\frac{4 R}{3} \\ & \text{ at } h=\frac{4 R}{3}, \frac{d^2 V}{d h^2} < 0 \end{aligned} $$ Hence at $h=\frac{4 R}{3}$, volume of cone is maximum. $$ \begin{aligned} & \frac{\text{ Volume of cone }}{\text{ Volume of sphere }}=\frac{\frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h}{\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3}=\frac{\left(2 h R-h^2\right) h}{4 R^3} \\ & =\frac{\left(\frac{8 R^2}{3}-\frac{16 R^2}{9}\right) \frac{4 R}{3}}{4 R^3}=\frac{8}{27} \end{aligned} $$

6298.text: If $f(x)=(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)$ for $x \in[0,4]$, then the value of $c \in(0,4)$ satisfying Lagrange's mean value theorem, is
6298.sol:
We have, $\begin{aligned}& f(x)=(x-1)(x-2)(x-3) \\
& f(x)=x³-6 x²+11 x-6
\end{aligned} Given function is algebraic function so. it is continuous$ and difference in[0,4]$ Now, \begin{aligned} f(4) & =(4)^3-6(4)^2+11(4)-6 \\
& =64-96+44-6=6 \\
f(0) & =-6
\end{aligned} Now, $ f^{\prime}(x)=3 x^2-12 x+11$
by Lagrange's mean value theorem \begin{aligned} f^{\prime}(c) & =\frac{f(4)-f(0)}{4-0}\\
\Rightarrow \quad 3 c²-12 c+11 & =\frac{6-(-6)}{4}\\
\Rightarrow \quad 3 c²-12 c+11 & =\frac{12}{4}\\
\Rightarrow 3 c²-12 c+11-3 & =0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad 3 c²-12 c+8 & =0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad c & =\frac{12 \pm \sqrt{(-12)^2-4(3)(8)}}{2 \times 3}\\
& =\frac{12 \pm \sqrt{144-96}}{6}=\frac{12 \pm 4 \sqrt{3}}{6}\\
c & =2 \pm \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{3} \in[0,4)
\end{aligned}
$

\(=\left(\alpha_$1+2 \alpha_3+\alpha_5\right)\left(\alpha_$2+\alpha_5+1\right)\left(\alpha_$4+1\right)-1\)
And, number of non-trivial odd divisors

7140.text: The sum of the minimum and maximum distance of the point $(4,-3)$ to the circle $x^2+y^2+4 x-10 y-7=0$, is

Centre of circle $=\mathrm{C}(-2,5)\text{ Radius }=\sqrt{(-2)^2+(5)^2+7}=\sqrt{4+25+7}=\sqrt{36}=6$
Maximum distance, $a=C P+r$
Minimum distance, $b=C P-r$
Sum of the maximum and minimum distance,
$a+b=C P+r+C P-r=2 C P$
and $C P=\sqrt{(-2-4)^2+(5+3)^2}=\sqrt{36+64}=\sqrt{100}=10$
Thus, $\quad a+b=2 C P=2 \times 10=20$

8208.text:
The solution of the differential equation $(2 x-4 y+3) \frac{d y}{d x}+(x-2 y+1)=0$ is
(C$ is an arbitrary constant)$
8208.sol:
Given differential equation,
$\begin{aligned}
& (2 x-4 y+3) \frac{d y}{d x}+(x-2 y+1)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{(x-2 y+1)}{2(x-2 y+3)} \quad \ldots \text{ (i) }
\end{aligned}$
Let, $x-2 y=v \Rightarrow 1-2 \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d y}{d x}\therefore \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{d y}{d x}\right)=\frac{d y}{d x}$
Now, substitute v=x-2 y and $\frac{d y}{d x}$ in eq. (i) integration both the sides, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{d v}{d x}\right)=-\left(\frac{v+1}{2 v+3}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d v}{d x}=1+\frac{2 v+2}{2 v+3} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{2 v+2}{4 v+5} d v=d x \\
& \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{4 v+6}{4 v+5} d v=\int d x \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \int\left(\frac{4 v+6}{4 v+5}+\frac{1}{4 v+5}\right) d v=\int d x \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} v+\frac{1}{2 \times 4} \log [4 v+5]=x+C \\
& \Rightarrow 4 v+\log [4 v+5]=8 x+C \\
& \Rightarrow 4(x-2 y)+\log [4(x-2 y)+5]=8 x+C \\
& \Rightarrow \log [4(x-2 y)+5]=4(x+2 y)+C
\end{aligned}$

12980.sol:
To get $\cot \frac{\pi}{24}\), we proceed as follows
\begin{aligned}
\cot\frac{\pi}{24}& =\frac{2 \cos ^2 \frac{\pi}{24}}{2 \sin \frac{\pi}{24} \cdot \cos \frac{\pi}{24}}\\
& =\frac{1+\cos \frac{\pi}{12}}{\sin \frac{\pi}{12}}=\frac{1+\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)}{1+\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)}
\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}& =\frac{1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{1}{2}}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{1}{2}}\\
& =2+\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{6}\\
& \text{and } \tan \frac{\pi}{24}=-2+\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{6}\\
& \text{So, } \frac{1}{2}\left(\tan \frac{\pi}{24}+\cot \frac{\pi}{24}\right)=\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}=\sqrt{2^2+2}+\sqrt{2}\\
& =\sqrt{a^2+a}+\sqrt{a} \quad \text{ (given) }\\
\end{aligned}\)
So, \(a=2\)$

13571.text: If the emf of an AC source is given by $6 \sin \omega t+4 \sin 2 \omega t \mathrm{ V}$, then the rms value of the emf is
13571.sol:
Given, emf of an AC source, $\begin{aligned}& \quad E=6 \sin \omegat+4 \sin 2 \omegat \\
& \text{ Now, } \quadE^2=(6 \sin \omegat+4 \sin 2 \omegat)^2 \\
& \therefore E²=36 \sin ^2 2 \omegat+16 \sin ^2 2 \omegat+48 \sin \omegat \cdot \sin2 \omegat \\
& =36 \sin ^2 \omegat+16 \sin ^2 2 \omegat+48\left(\cos \frac{\omega t}{2}-\cos \frac{3 \omega t}{2}\right)
\end{aligned}$ Now, the average value of $E^2$, $\begin{aligned}& \therefore \quad E_{\text{avg }}=\frac{1}{T} \int_0^T\left[E^2 d t\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{T} \int_0^T\left[36 \sin ^2 \omegat+16 \sin ^2 2 \omegat+48\left(\frac{\cos \omega t}{2}-\frac{\cos 3 \omega t}{2}\right)\right]\\
& =\frac{1}{T}\left[36 \cdot \frac{T}{2}+16 \times \frac{T}{2}+48(0-0)\right] \\
& \text{ or } \quadE_{\text{avg }}=18+8=26 \mathrm{ V}\\
& \therefore \quad E_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{E_{\mathrm{avg}}}=\sqrt{26} \mathrm{ V}\\
&
\end{aligned} So, the rms value of emf is \sqrt{26} \mathrm{ V} .$

${f}_{0} = \dfrac{v}{2l} = \dfrac{\dfrac{mg}{μ}}{2l} ⇒ m = \dfrac{4l^{2}{f0}^{2}\mu}{g} = \dfrac{4 \times 1 \times {10}^{4} \times 2 \times {10}^{- 3}}{10} = 8kg$

22810.text: A particle of mass 3 g and charge $60 \mu \mathrm{C}$ is released from rest in a uniform electric field of intensity $10^5 N C^{-1}$. If the value of kinetic energy attained by the particle after moving through a distance of 2 cm is $m \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{ J}$, then the value of m is:
22810.sol:
Given mass $m = 3 \text{ g} = 3 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kg}$, charge $q = 60 \mu \text{C} = 60 \times 10^{-6} \text{ C}$, electric field $E = 10^5 \text{ N C}^{-1}$, and distance $d = 2 \text{ cm} = 0.02 \text{ m}$.

The force acting on the particle is $F = qE = (60 \times 10^{-6} \text{ C}) \times (10^5 \text{ N C}^{-1}) = 6 \text{ N}$.

The work done by the electric field on the particle is $W = F \times d = 6 \text{ N} \times 0.02 \text{ m} = 0.12 \text{ J}$.

According to the work-energy theorem, the kinetic energy attained by the particle starting from rest is equal to the work done by the electric field.

Kinetic Energy $K = 0.12 \text{ J} = 12 \times 10^{-2} \text{ J}$.

Comparing this with the given expression $m \times 10^{-2} \text{ J}$, we find $m = 12$.

Answer: $12$

23176.subject: Physics
23176.text: A man grows into a giant such that his height increases to 8 times his original height. Assuming that his density remains same, the stress in the leg will change by a factor of
23176.sol:
Let the original height of the man be $h$ and the original cross-sectional area of his legs be $A$. The mass of the man is $m = \rho V$, where $\rho$ is the density and $V$ is the volume. Since the man grows geometrically similar, the volume $V$ is proportional to $h^3$. Thus, $m \propto h^3$.

The stress $\sigma$ in the legs is defined as the force per unit area, $\sigma = \dfrac{F}{A} = \dfrac{mg}{A}$.

Since the man grows geometrically similar, the cross-sectional area $A$ of the legs scales as $h^2$.

Substituting the scaling relations $m \propto h^3$ and $A \propto h^2$ into the stress formula, we get $\sigma \propto \dfrac{h^3}{h^2} = h$.

Given that the height increases by a factor of 8, the stress in the legs will also increase by a factor of 8.

Answer: 8

27200.subject: Chemistry
27200.text: The correct stability order of the following diazonium salts is
27200.sol:
The stability of benzenediazonium salts is governed by the electronic effects of the substituents present on the benzene ring.
The diazonium group $-N_2^+$ is strongly electron-withdrawing. Electron-donating groups (EDG) stabilize the diazonium cation by dispersing the positive charge through resonance or inductive effects, whereas electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) destabilize it by increasing the positive charge density.
In (A), the $-OCH_3$ group at the para position is a strong electron-donating group via the $+M$ effect, which significantly stabilizes the diazonium ion.
In (C), there is no substituent (hydrogen), providing a baseline stability.
In (D), the $-CN$ group is an electron-withdrawing group via $-M$ and $-I$ effects, which destabilizes the cation.
In (B), the $-NO_2$ group is a very strong electron-withdrawing group via $-M$ and $-I$ effects, even stronger than $-CN$, leading to the least stability.
Comparing the effects: $+M$ of $-OCH_3$ (A) > $H$ (C) > $-M$ of $-CN$ (D) > $-M$ of $-NO_2$ (B).
Therefore, the correct stability order is $A > C > D > B$.

32152.subject: Chemistry
32152.text: The Bohr radius of a hydrogen like species is $70.53$ pm. The species and the stationary state $(n)$ are respectively (Given : Hydrogen atom Bohr radius is $52.9$ pm)
32152.sol:
The radius of the $n$-th Bohr orbit for a hydrogen-like species is given by the formula:

$r_n = a_0 \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$

where $a_0$ is the Bohr radius of the hydrogen atom ($52.9$ pm), $n$ is the principal quantum number, and $Z$ is the atomic number.

Given $r_n = 70.53$ pm, we can write:

$70.53 = 52.9 \times \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$

$\dfrac{n^2}{Z} = \dfrac{70.53}{52.9} = 1.333 = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Checking the given options:
For $\text{Li}^{2+}$ and $n = 3$, $Z = 3 \Rightarrow \dfrac{n^2}{Z} = \dfrac{9}{3} = 3$
For $\text{He}^+$ and $n = 3$, $Z = 2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{n^2}{Z} = \dfrac{9}{2} = 4.5$
For $\text{He}^+$ and $n = 2$, $Z = 2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{n^2}{Z} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2$
For $\text{Li}^{2+}$ and $n = 2$, $Z = 3 \Rightarrow \dfrac{n^2}{Z} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

The ratio matches for $\text{Li}^{2+}$ and $n = 2$.

Answer: $\text{Li}^{2+}, 2$

35957.subject: Mathematics
35957.text: Let $M$ be a $3 \times 3$ matrix such that $M \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$, $M \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$ and $M \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$. If $M \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 7 \\ 11 \end{pmatrix}$, then $x + y + z$ equals :
35957.sol:
Let $M$ be the matrix whose columns are the given vectors. We have:

$M = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$

Given $M \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 7 \\ 11 \end{pmatrix}$, we can write this as a system of linear equations:

$x - z = 1$

$2x + y + z = 7$

$3x + 2y + z = 11$

Subtracting the second equation from the third equation gives:

$x + y = 4$

Adding the first equation and the second equation gives:

$3x + y = 8$

Subtracting the equation $x + y = 4$ from $3x + y = 8$ gives:

$2x = 4 \Rightarrow x = 2$

Substituting $x = 2$ into $x + y = 4$ gives:

$2 + y = 4 \Rightarrow y = 2$

Substituting $x = 2$ into $x - z = 1$ gives:

$2 - z = 1 \Rightarrow z = 1$

Therefore, $x + y + z = 2 + 2 + 1 = 5$.

Answer: $5$

35959.text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 7 \\ 4 & -2 & 8 \\ 3 & 8 & -7 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\det(A-\alpha I)=0$, where $\alpha$ is a real number. If the largest possible value of $\alpha$ is $p$, then the circle $(x-p)^2+(y-2p)^2=320$, intersects the co-ordinate axes at
35959.sol:
The characteristic equation is given by $\det(A-\alpha I) = 0$.

$\det \begin{bmatrix} 1-\alpha & 2 & 7 \\ 4 & -2-\alpha & 8 \\ 3 & 8 & -7-\alpha \end{bmatrix} = 0$

Expanding the determinant along the first row:

$(1-\alpha)[(-2-\alpha)(-7-\alpha) - 64] - 2[4(-7-\alpha) - 24] + 7[32 - 3(-2-\alpha)] = 0$

$(1-\alpha)(\alpha^2 + 9\alpha - 50) - 2(-4\alpha - 52) + 7(3\alpha + 38) = 0$

$-\alpha^3 - 8\alpha^2 + 59\alpha - 50 + 8\alpha + 104 + 21\alpha + 266 = 0$

$\alpha^3 + 8\alpha^2 - 88\alpha - 320 = 0$

By inspection, $\alpha = 8$ is a root since $8^3 + 8(8^2) - 88(8) - 320 = 512 + 512 - 704 - 320 = 0$.

Factoring out $(\alpha - 8)$, we get:

$(\alpha - 8)(\alpha^2 + 16\alpha + 40) = 0$

The roots are $\alpha = 8$ and $\alpha = \dfrac{-16 \pm \sqrt{256 - 160}}{2} = -8 \pm 2\sqrt{6}$.

The largest possible value of $\alpha$ is $p = 8$.

Substituting $p = 8$ into the given equation of the circle:

$(x-8)^2 + (y-16)^2 = 320$

To find the intersection points with the x-axis, substitute $y = 0$:

$(x-8)^2 + (-16)^2 = 320$

$(x-8)^2 + 256 = 320 \Rightarrow (x-8)^2 = 64 \Rightarrow x-8 = \pm 8$

$x = 0$ or $x = 16$

The circle intersects the x-axis at $(0, 0)$ and $(16, 0)$.

To find the intersection points with the y-axis, substitute $x = 0$:

$(-8)^2 + (y-16)^2 = 320$

$64 + (y-16)^2 = 320 \Rightarrow (y-16)^2 = 256 \Rightarrow y-16 = \pm 16$

$y = 0$ or $y = 32$

The circle intersects the y-axis at $(0, 0)$ and $(0, 32)$.

The distinct points of intersection with the coordinate axes are $(0, 0)$, $(16, 0)$, and $(0, 32)$.

Thus, the circle intersects the coordinate axes at exactly $3$ points.

Answer: $3$ points

36343.text: The number of strictly increasing functions $f$ from the set $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ to the set $\{1,2,3, \ldots., 9\}$ such that $f(i) \neq i$ for $1 \leq i \leq 6$, is equal to :
36343.sol:
For strictly increasing $f$, if we choose elements $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_6$, then $f(i) = a_i$.
Since $f(i) \geq i$ always, condition $f(i) \neq i$ means $f(i) \geq i + 1$ for all $i$.
Let $h(i) = f(i) - i$. Then $h(i) \geq 1$, $h(6) \leq 3$, and $h$ is non-decreasing.
So $h(i) \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ for all $i$.
Number of non-decreasing sequences of length 6 from $\{1, 2, 3\} = \binom{8}{2} = 28$.

36890.text: Let $f\left(x\right)$ be a quadratic polynomial with leading coefficient $1$ such that $f\left(0\right) = p, p \ne 0$, and $f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$. If the equations $f\left(x\right) = 0$ and $fofofof\left(x\right) = 0$ have a common real root, then $f\left(- 3\right)$ is equal to ______.
36890.sol:
Let $f\left(x\right) = \left(x - \alpha\right)\left(x - \beta\right)$

It is given that $f\left(0\right) = p ⇒ \alpha\beta = p$

and $f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{3} ⇒ \left(1 - \alpha\right)\left(1 - \beta\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Now let us assume that $\alpha$ is the common root of $f\left(x\right) = 0$ and $fofofof\left(x\right) = 0$

$fofofof\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ fofofof\left(\alpha\right) = 0$

$⇒ fofof\left(0\right) = 0$

$⇒ fof\left(p\right) = 0$

So, $f\left(p\right)$ is either $\alpha$ or $\beta$.

Now assuming $\left(p - \alpha\right)\left(p - \beta\right) = \alpha$

$⇒ \left(\alpha\beta - \alpha\right)\left(\alpha\beta - \beta\right) = \alpha ⇒ \left(\beta - 1\right)\left(\alpha - 1\right)\beta = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{\beta}{3} = 1$ $\left(\text{as}\left(1 - \alpha\right)\left(1 - \beta\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

So, $\beta = 3$

Now finding $\alpha$ by putting the value of $\beta\text{in}\left(1 - \alpha\right)\left(1 - \beta\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$,

$⇒ \left(1 - \alpha\right)\left(1 - 3\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{7}{6}$

So, $f\left(x\right) = \left(x - \dfrac{7}{6}\right)\left(x - 3\right)$

So, $f\left(- 3\right) = \left(- 3 - \dfrac{7}{6}\right)\left(- 3 - 3\right) = 25$

$\begin{aligned}$& x=$\sqrt{\lambda}$y+($\sqrt{\lambda}-$1) \Rightarrow y=$\frac{x-(\sqrt{\lambda}-1)}{\sqrt{\lambda}}$\\
& z=($\sqrt{\lambda}-$1) y+$\sqrt{\lambda} \Rightarrow$y=$\frac{z-\sqrt{\lambda}}{\sqrt{\lambda}-1}
\end{aligned}$From (i) and (ii)

$\frac{x-(\sqrt{\lambda}-1)}{\sqrt{\lambda}}=\frac{y-0}{1}=\frac{z-\sqrt{\lambda}}{\sqrt{\lambda}-1}$The equation (A) is the equation of line $\mathrm{L}_1$. Similarly equation of line $\mathrm{L}_2$ is

$\frac{x-(1-\sqrt{\mu})}{\sqrt{\mu}}=\frac{y-0}{1}=\frac{z-\sqrt{\mu}}{1-\sqrt{\mu}}$Since $\mathrm{L}_1 \perp \mathrm{L}_2$, therefore

$\begin{aligned}$& $\sqrt{\lambda} \sqrt{\mu}+$1 $\times$1+($\sqrt{\lambda}-$1)(1-$\sqrt{\mu})=$0 \\
& \Rightarrow $\sqrt{\lambda}+\sqrt{\mu}=$0 \Rightarrow $\sqrt{\lambda}=-\sqrt{\mu}$\\
& \Rightarrow \lambda=\mu
\end{aligned}

38130.text: If the shortest distance between the lines $\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right), \lambda \in R, \alpha > 0$ and $\overset{\to}{{r}_{2}} = - 4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k} + \mu\left(3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right), \mu \in R$ is $9,$ then $\alpha$ is equal to_____.
38130.sol:
We have,

$\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{\to}{{r}_{2}} = - 4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k} + \mu\left(3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

If $\overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{a} + \lambda\overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{c} + \lambda\overset{\to}{d}$, then shortest distance between two lines is

$L = \dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{c}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right|}$

Here,

$\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & 2 \\ 3 & - 2 & - 2\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d} = 8\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d} = 4\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right| = 4 \cdot 3$

And,

$\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{c} = \left(\left(\alpha + 4\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

So, shortest distance is

$\dfrac{\left(\left(\alpha + 4\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot 4\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{4 \cdot 3} = 9$

$⇒ 2\left(\alpha + 4\right) + 4 + 3 = 27$

$⇒ \left(\alpha + 4\right) = 10$

$⇒ \alpha = 6$

38335.text: The sum of solutions of the equation $\dfrac{cosx}{1 + sinx} = \left|tan2x\right|, x \in \left(- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \left\{- \dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right\}$ is:
38335.sol:
We have,

$\dfrac{cosx}{1 + sinx} = \left|tan2x\right|$

where, $x \in \left(\dfrac{- \pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{- \pi}{4}\right\}$

Case-$1:$ When $0 \le x < \dfrac{\pi}{4} \text{ and } - \dfrac{\pi}{2} < x < - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

$\dfrac{cosx}{1 + sinx} = tan2x$

$⇒ \dfrac{cosx}{1 + sinx} = \dfrac{sin2x}{cos2x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{cosx}{1 + sinx} = \dfrac{2sinxcosx}{\cos^{2}x - \sin^{2}x}$

$⇒ cosx\left(\cos^{2}x - \sin^{2}x\right) = 2sinxcosx\left(1 + sinx\right)$

$⇒ cosx\left(1 - 2\sin^{2}x\right) = cosx\left(2sinx + 2\sin^{2}x\right)$

$⇒ cosx\left(- 4\sin^{2}x - 2sinx + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ cosx\left(4\sin^{2}x + 2sinx - 1\right) = 0$

Then,

$cosx = 0$ (Not possible, since $0 \le x < \dfrac{\pi}{4} \text{ and } - \dfrac{\pi}{2} < x < - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$)

And,

$sinx = \dfrac{- 2 \pm 2\sqrt{5}}{8} = \dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{4}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{\pi}{10}, \dfrac{- 3\pi}{10}$

Case-$2:$ When $\dfrac{\pi}{4} < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\dfrac{- \pi}{4} < x < 0$, then

$\dfrac{cosx}{1 + sinx} = - tan2x$

$⇒ \dfrac{cosx}{1 + sinx} = \dfrac{- sin2x}{cos2x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{cosx}{1 + sinx} = \dfrac{- 2sinxcosx}{\cos^{2}x - \sin^{2}x}$

$⇒ cosx\left(\cos^{2}x - \sin^{2}x\right) = - 2sinxcosx\left(1 + sinx\right)$

$⇒ cosx\left(1 - 2\sin^{2}x\right) = cosx\left(- 2sinx - 2\sin^{2}x\right)$

$⇒ cosx ( 1 + 2sinx ) = 0$

$⇒ cosx = 0 ⇒ x \in ϕ$

And, $sinx = \dfrac{- 1}{2} ⇒ x = \dfrac{- \pi}{6}$

Sum of solutions

$= \dfrac{\pi}{10} - \dfrac{3\pi}{10} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{- 11\pi}{30}$

$⇒ 10\lambda - 2\mu = 56$

39004.text: In a hydrogen spectrum $\lambda$ be the wavelength of first transition line of Lyman series. The wavelength difference will be "$a\lambda$" between the wavelength of ${3}^{rd}$ transition line of Paschen series and that of ${2}^{nd}$ transition line of Balmer Series where $a =$ _____.
39004.sol:
Using Rydberg formula,

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R\left(1{n}_{f}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{{n}_{i}^{2}}\right)$, where, $R$ is Rydberg constant and $n$ is quantum number.

For first line of Lyman series

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) = R\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{4}{3R} . . . \left(1\right)$

For ${3}^{rd}$ line of Paschen series

$\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{3}} = R\left(\dfrac{1}{{3}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{6}^{2}}\right) = \dfrac{R}{9} \times \dfrac{3}{4}$

For ${2}^{nd}$ line of Balmer series

$\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{2}} = R\left(\dfrac{1}{{2}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{4}^{2}}\right) = \dfrac{R}{4} \times \dfrac{3}{4}$

Thus, $a\lambda = {\lambda}_{3} - {\lambda}_{2} = \dfrac{12}{R} - \dfrac{16}{3R} = \dfrac{20}{3R}$

Putting equation $\left(1\right)$

$a\left(\dfrac{4}{3R}\right) = \dfrac{20}{3R} ⇒ a = 5$

39520.subject: Physics
39520.text: In the potentiometer, when the cell in the secondary circuit is shunted with $4 \Omega$ resistance, the balance is obtained at the length 120 cm of wire. Now when the same cell is shunted with $12 \Omega$ resistance, the balance is shifted to a length of 180 cm. The internal resistance of cell is $\_\_\_\_$ $\Omega$
39520.sol:
In a potentiometer, the internal resistance $r$ of a cell is given by the formula $r = R \left( \frac{l_0}{l} - 1 \right)$, where $l_0$ is the balancing length in open circuit, $l$ is the balancing length when shunted with resistance $R$.
This can be rewritten as $\frac{l_0}{l} = 1 + \frac{r}{R}$ or $l = \frac{l_0}{1 + r/R}$.
Case 1: $R_1 = 4 \Omega$ and $l_1 = 120$ cm.
$120 = \frac{l_0}{1 + r/4} = \frac{4l_0}{4 + r}$ ... (i)
Case 2: $R_2 = 12 \Omega$ and $l_2 = 180$ cm.
$180 = \frac{l_0}{1 + r/12} = \frac{12l_0}{12 + r}$ ... (ii)
Dividing equation (ii) by (i):
$\frac{180}{120} = \frac{12l_0}{12 + r} \times \frac{4 + r}{4l_0}$
$\frac{3}{2} = \frac{3(4 + r)}{12 + r}$
$\frac{1}{2} = \frac{4 + r}{12 + r}$
$12 + r = 8 + 2r$
$r = 4 \Omega$
The internal resistance of the cell is $4 \Omega$.

Paragraph: Consider a block of conducting material of resistivity ' $\rho$ ' shown in the figure. Current 'l' enters at 'A' and leaves from ' $\mathrm{D}$ '. We apply superposition principle to find voltage ' $\Delta \mathrm{V}$ ' developed between ' $\mathrm{B}$ ' and ' $\mathrm{C}$ '. The calculation is done in the following steps: (i) Take current 'l' entering from 'A' and assume it to spread over a hemispherical surface in the block. (ii) Calculate field $E(r)$ at distance ' $r$ ' from $A$ by using Ohm's law $E=\rho j$, where $j$ is the current per unit area at ' $r$ '. (iii) From the ' $r$ ' dependence of $E(r)$, obtain the potential $V(r)$ at $r$. (iv) Repeat (i), (ii) and (iii) for current 'l' leaving ' $D$ ' and superpose results for ' $A$ ' and ' $D$ '.
Question: $\Delta \mathrm{V}$ measured between $\mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ is
options:
$\frac{\rho l}{\pi a}-\frac{\rho l}{\pi(a+b)}$

$\frac{\rho l}{a}-\frac{\rho l}{(a+b)}$

$\frac{\rho l}{2 \pi a}-\frac{\rho l}{2 \pi(a+b)}$

$\frac{\rho l}{2 \pi(a-b)}$
39873.sol:
Choosing $A$ as origin,
$$
\begin{gathered}
E=\rho j=\rho \frac{1}{2 \pi r^2} \\
V_C-V_B=-\frac{\rho l}{2 \pi} \int_a^{(a+b)} \frac{1}{r^2} d r=\frac{\rho l}{2 \pi}\left[\frac{1}{(a+b)}-\frac{1}{a}\right] \\
V_B-V_C=\frac{\rho l}{2 \pi}\left[\frac{1}{a}-\frac{1}{(a+b)}\right]
\end{gathered}
$$

39979.text: The threshold frequency of metal is ${f}_{0}$. When the light of frequency $2{f}_{0}$ is incident on the metal plate, the maximum velocity of photoelectron is ${v}_{1}$. When the frequency of incident radiation is increased to $5{f}_{0}$. the maximum velocity of photoelectrons emitted is ${v}_{2}$. The ratio of ${v}_{1}$ to ${v}_{2}$ is:
39979.sol:
Maximum kinetic energy is related to the incident frequency $f$ and the threshold frequency ${f}_{0}$ as:

${K}_{max} = hf - h{f}_{0}$

When, $f = 2{f}_{0}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} = 2h{f}_{0} - h{f}_{0} = h{f}_{0} . . . \left(1\right)$

When, $f = 5{f}_{0}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{2}^{2} = 5h{f}_{0} - h{f}_{0} = 4h{f}_{0} . . . \left(2\right)$

Hence, the ratio, $\dfrac{{v}_{1}}{{v}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

41949.text: $64$ identical drops each charged upto potential of $10mV$ are combined to form a bigger drop. The potential of the bigger drop will be _____ $mV$.
41949.sol:
The formula to calculate the potential $\left(V\right)$ of each tiny drop is given by

$V = k\dfrac{q}{r} . . . \left(1\right)$

When all the drops forms the bigger drop the radius of the new drop $\left(r '\right)$ can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}Volumeofbigdrop & = & 64 \times volumeofeachtinydrop \\ ⇒ & \dfrac{4}{3}\pir{'}^{3} = 64 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3} \\ ⇒ & r ' = 4r\end{cases}$

So, the potential of the new big drop $\left(V '\right)$ can be written as

$\begin{cases}V ' & = & k\dfrac{64q}{r '} \\ = & k\dfrac{64q}{4r} \\ = & 16k\dfrac{q}{r} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and simplify to obtain the potential of the new drop.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{V '}{V} & = & \dfrac{16k\dfrac{q}{r}}{k\dfrac{q}{r}} \\ ⇒ & V ' = 16V . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the value of the known parameter into equation (3) to calculate the required value of the potential for the new drop.

$\begin{cases}V ' & = & 16 \times 10mV \\ = & 160mV\end{cases}$

42870.subject: Physics
42870.text: The size of the images of an object, formed by a thin lens are equal when the object is placed at two different positions 8 cm and 24 cm from the lens. The focal length of the lens is $\_\_\_\_$ cm.
42870.sol:
The magnification of a thin lens is given by $m = \frac{f}{f + u}$.
Given that the size of the images is equal for two different object positions, the magnitudes of the magnifications must be equal: $|m_1| = |m_2|$.
For a single lens to produce images of the same size at two different object distances, one image must be real and the other must be virtual.
Let $u_1 = -8$ cm and $u_2 = -24$ cm.
Then, $m_1 = -m_2$ (since one is real and one is virtual).
$\frac{f}{f + u_1} = -\frac{f}{f + u_2}$
$\frac{1}{f - 8} = -\frac{1}{f - 24}$
$f - 24 = -(f - 8)$
$f - 24 = -f + 8$
$2f = 32$
$f = 16$ cm.
The focal length of the lens is 16 cm.

At -43°C, the temperature drop from 27°C is $\Delta T_1 = 70°C$
It creates tension $T = YA\alpha\Delta T_1$ where $Y$ is Young's modulus and $\alpha$ is linear expansion coefficient.
For tension to increase to $1.4T$, the new temperature drop must be: $\Delta T_2 = 1.4 \times 70 = 98°C$.
Required temperature: $T_3 = 27 - 98 = -71°C$

50231.text: A horizontal force of $5$ N is applied on a stationary body of mass $5$ kg, which is initially at rest on a frictionless table. The change in kinetic energy of the body in $10$ s is

Horizontal force $F = 5$ N

Acceleration of the body $a = \dfrac{F}{m} = \dfrac{5}{5} = 1$ m/s$^2$

Initial velocity $u = 0$

Time $t = 10$ s

Using the equation of motion $v = u + at$,

$v = 0 + 1 \times 10 = 10$ m/s

Initial kinetic energy $K_i = 0$

Final kinetic energy $K_f = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times (10)^2 = 250$ J

Change in kinetic energy $\Delta K = K_f - K_i = 250 - 0 = 250$ J

Answer: $250$ J

& \alpha^2+p \alpha+q=0 \text{ and } \alpha^2+q \alpha+p=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\alpha^2}{p^2-q^2}=\frac{\alpha}{q-p}=\frac{1}{q-p}
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \alpha^2=\frac{(p-q)(p+q)}{-(p-q)}=-(p+q) \ldots$...(iii)
and $\quad \alpha=\frac{q-p}{q-p}=1$ ...(iv)
$\therefore$ From Eq. (iii)
$\begin{aligned} & & \alpha^2 & =-p+q \\ \Rightarrow & & (1)^2 & =-(p+q) \quad[\text{ from Eq. (iv) }] \\ \Rightarrow & & p+q & =-1 \Rightarrow p+q+1=0\end{aligned}$

55252.text: Which from following amines does NOT form alkyl isocyanide when heated with alc. KOH and chloroform
55252.sol:
The reaction of an amine with chloroform and alcoholic KOH to form an alkyl isocyanide is known as the carbylamine reaction.

This test is given only by primary (aliphatic and aromatic) amines. Secondary and tertiary amines do not respond to this test.

Methanamine, propan-2-amine, and ethanamine are primary amines, so they will form alkyl isocyanides.

N, N-Diethylethanamine is a tertiary amine, hence it does not undergo the carbylamine reaction and will not form an alkyl isocyanide.

55260.subject: Chemistry
55260.text: Which of the following amines is not represented by formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ ?
55260.sol:
The molecular formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ corresponds to saturated acyclic amines.

The possible structural isomers are:

Primary ($1^{}^{\circ}$) amines: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (propan-1-amine) and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)\text{CH}_3$ (propan-2-amine).

Secondary ($2^{}^{\circ}$) amine: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NHCH}_3$ (N-methylethanamine).

Tertiary ($3^{}^{\circ}$) amine: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$ (N,N-dimethylmethanamine).

A quaternary ammonium salt requires the nitrogen atom to be bonded to four alkyl groups. The simplest quaternary ammonium salt is the tetramethylammonium ion, which contains four carbon atoms ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{12}\text{N}^+$).

Thus, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ cannot represent a quaternary ammonium salt.

Answer: quaternary ammonium salt

58240.text: What is shape of interhalogen compound so that central halogen exhibits +3 oxidation state?
58240.sol:
Consider $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ where chlorine exhibits a +3 oxidation state. Fluorine's -1 oxidation state gives a total of -3, balanced by chlorine's +3 state.

Chlorine has 7 valence electrons. Bonding with three fluorine atoms uses 3 electrons, leaving 4 electrons that form 2 lone pairs. The total electron pairs are 5, resulting in a trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry.

Lone pairs occupy equatorial positions to minimize repulsion, forcing the three bonding pairs into a T-shaped molecular geometry.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

59148.text: $Calculate the osmotic pressure of 0.2 M aqueous solution of electrolyte at 300 K. If van't Hoff factor is 1.6  \left[\mathrm{R}=0.0821 \mathrm{ atm} \mathrm{dm}^3 \mathrm{ K}^{-1} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}\right]$
59148.sol:
The osmotic pressure $\Pi$ of an electrolyte solution is given by the van't Hoff equation $\Pi = iCRT$, where $i$ is the van't Hoff factor, $C$ is the molar concentration, $R$ is the gas constant, and $T$ is the absolute temperature.

Substituting the given values $i = 1.6$, $C = 0.2 \text{ M}$, $R = 0.0821 \text{ dm}^3 \text{ atm K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$, and $T = 300 \text{ K}$:

$\Pi = 1.6 \times 0.2 \times 0.0821 \times 300 = 7.8816 \text{ atm}$

Rounded to two decimal places, the osmotic pressure is $7.88 \text{ atm}$, which corresponds to option B.

61029.subject: Mathematics
61029.sol:
Let $I = \int_0^\pi \dfrac{1}{1 + 2^{\cos x}} \, dx$

Using the property $\int_0^a f(x) \, dx = \int_0^a f(a-x) \, dx$, we get:

$I = \int_0^\pi \dfrac{1}{1 + 2^{\cos(\pi - x)}} \, dx$

$I = \int_0^\pi \dfrac{1}{1 + 2^{-\cos x}} \, dx$

$I = \int_0^\pi \dfrac{2^{\cos x}}{2^{\cos x} + 1} \, dx$

Adding the two equations for $I$:

$2I = \int_0^\pi \left( \dfrac{1}{1 + 2^{\cos x}} + \dfrac{2^{\cos x}}{1 + 2^{\cos x}} \right) \, dx$

$2I = \int_0^\pi 1 \, dx$

$2I = \pi$

$I = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

62159.subject: Mathematics
62159.text: Let $f(x) = x$, $f_1(x) = f(\log x)$, $f_2(x) = f_1(\log x)$, $f_3(x) = f_2(\log x)$, $\ldots$ and so on. Then $\int \dfrac{1}{f(x)\,f_1(x)\,f_2(x)\,\ldots f_{2026}(x)}\,dx = \ldots$
62159.sol:
Given $f(x) = x$

$f_1(x) = f(\log x) = \log x$

$f_2(x) = f_1(\log x) = \log(\log x)$

In general, $f_n(x) = \log(f_{n-1}(x))$.

Differentiating $f_n(x)$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:

$f_1'(x) = \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{1}{f(x)}$

$f_2'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(\log(f_1(x))) = \dfrac{1}{f_1(x)} f_1'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f_1(x) f(x)}$

$f_3'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(\log(f_2(x))) = \dfrac{1}{f_2(x)} f_2'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f_2(x) f_1(x) f(x)}$

By induction, $f_n'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f_{n-1}(x) f_{n-2}(x) \ldots f_1(x) f(x)}$.

For $n = 2027$, we have:

$f_{2027}'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f_{2026}(x) f_{2025}(x) \ldots f_1(x) f(x)}$

The given integral is:

$I = \int \dfrac{1}{f(x) f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_{2026}(x)} \, dx$

$I = \int f_{2027}'(x) \, dx$

$I = f_{2027}(x) + c$

Answer: $f_{2027}(x) + c$

62227.sol:
Let $I = \int \frac{\sin 2x \cos 2x}{\sqrt{4 - \cos^4 2x}} dx$.

Applying the substitution $u = \cos^2 2x$, the differential becomes $du = -4 \sin 2x \cos 2x dx$, yielding $\sin 2x \cos 2x dx = -\frac{1}{4} du$.

Substituting into the integral gives $I = -\frac{1}{4} \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - u^2}} du$.

This evaluates to the inverse sine form: $I = -\frac{1}{4} \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{u}{2}\right) + c$.

Returning to the original variable, $I = -\frac{1}{4} \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{\cos^2 2x}{2}\right) + c$.

62718.subject: Mathematics
62718.text: If $\mathrm{f}(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}\frac{9^x-2 \cdot 3^x+1}{\log(1+3 x) \cdot \tan 2 x} & , \text{ if } x \neq 0 \\ \mathrm{a}(\log \mathrm{b})^{\mathrm{c}} & , \text{ if } x=0\end{array}\right.$ is continuous at $x=0$, then $\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c}=$
62718.sol:
To ensure continuity at $x = 0$, the limit must satisfy $\lim_{x \to 0} f(x) = f(0)$.

Direct evaluation gives $f(0) = a (\log b)^c$.

The limit expression is $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{9^x - 2 \cdot 3^x + 1}{\log(1 + 3x) \cdot \tan 2x}$.
Factor the numerator: $9^x - 2 \cdot 3^x + 1 = (3^x - 1)^2$.

Rewriting the limit: $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{(3^x - 1)^2}{\log(1 + 3x) \cdot \tan 2x}$.

Using known limits $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{a^x - 1}{x} = \log a$, $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\log(1 + kx)}{x} = k$, and $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\tan kx}{x} = k$, divide by $x^2$:

$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\left(\frac{3^x - 1}{x}\right)^2}{\left(\frac{\log(1 + 3x)}{x}\right) \cdot \left(\frac{\tan 2x}{x}\right)} = \frac{(\log 3)^2}{3 \cdot 2} = \frac{(\log 3)^2}{6}$.

Setting $f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$ yields $a (\log b)^c = \frac{(\log 3)^2}{6}$.

Matching terms gives $a = \frac{1}{6}$, $b = 3$, and $c = 2$.

The sum is $a + b + c = \frac{1}{6} + 3 + 2 = \frac{31}{6}$.

$\boxed{\frac{31}{6}}$

64352.subject: Mathematics
64352.text: The perpendicular distance from the origin to the plane containing the points $(1, -2, 1), (2, -1, -3)$ and $(0, 1, 5)$ is...(in units)
64352.sol:
Let the given points be $A(1, -2, 1)$, $B(2, -1, -3)$ and $C(0, 1, 5)$.

The vectors in the plane are:
$\vec{AB} = (2 - 1)\hat{i} + (-1 - (-2))\hat{j} + (-3 - 1)\hat{k} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$
$\vec{AC} = (0 - 1)\hat{i} + (1 - (-2))\hat{j} + (5 - 1)\hat{k} = -\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$

The normal vector to the plane is given by the cross product $\vec{n} = \vec{AB} \times \vec{AC}$:
$\vec{n} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } -4 \\ -1 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 4 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(4 - (-12)) - \hat{j}(4 - 4) + \hat{k}(3 - (-1)) = 16\hat{i} + 4\hat{k}$

A simpler normal vector is $\vec{n}' = 4\hat{i} + \hat{k}$.

The equation of the plane passing through $A(1, -2, 1)$ with normal vector $4\hat{i} + \hat{k}$ is:
$4(x - 1) + 0(y - (-2)) + 1(z - 1) = 0$
$4x + z - 5 = 0$

The perpendicular distance from the origin $(0, 0, 0)$ to the plane $4x + z - 5 = 0$ is:
$d = \dfrac{|4(0) + 0(0) + 1(0) - 5|}{\sqrt{4^2 + 0^2 + 1^2}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{17}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{17}}$

64393.text: If a line makes angles $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ with the coordinate axes, then the sum of values of $\sin^2\alpha + \sin^2\beta + \sin^2\gamma$ and $\cos 2\alpha + \cos 2\beta + \cos 2\gamma$ is...
64393.sol:
The sum to be evaluated is $\sin^2\alpha + \sin^2\beta + \sin^2\gamma + \cos 2\alpha + \cos 2\beta + \cos 2\gamma$.

Using the trigonometric identity $\cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta$, we can write $\sin^2\theta + \cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta$.

Grouping the terms, we get:

$(\sin^2\alpha + \cos 2\alpha) + (\sin^2\beta + \cos 2\beta) + (\sin^2\gamma + \cos 2\gamma)$

$= \cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma$

Since $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are the angles made by a line with the coordinate axes, their direction cosines satisfy:

$\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1$

Thus, the required sum is $1$.

Answer: $1$

$\begin{aligned}

x & x-2 & -1
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 1(-1-x+2)+1(-1-x)+2(x-2-x)=0 \\
& \\
& \Rightarrow 1-x-1-x-4=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x=-2
\end{aligned}$

66321.subject: Physics
66321.text: In the following network, the current flowing through $15\ \Omega$ resistance is
66321.sol:
The given circuit is a Wheatstone bridge.

Checking the balance condition:
$\dfrac{R_{AB}}{R_{BC}} = \dfrac{15}{3} = 5$
$\dfrac{R_{AD}}{R_{DC}} = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5$

Since $\dfrac{R_{AB}}{R_{BC}} = \dfrac{R_{AD}}{R_{DC}}$, the bridge is balanced and no current flows through the $6\ \Omega$ resistor in branch BD.

The circuit simplifies to two parallel branches:
Resistance of the upper branch, $R_1 = 15 + 3 = 18\ \Omega$
Resistance of the lower branch, $R_2 = 20 + 4 = 24\ \Omega$

The total current is $I = 2.1\ \text{A}$.

Using the current divider rule, the current through the $15\ \Omega$ resistance (upper branch) is:
$I_{15\Omega} = I \times \dfrac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}$

$I_{15\Omega} = 2.1 \times \dfrac{24}{18 + 24}$

$I_{15\Omega} = 2.1 \times \dfrac{24}{42} = 1.2\ \text{A}$

Answer: $1.2$ A

67296.text: The mass and radius of the earth and moon are $M_1, R_1 and M_2, R_2$ respectively. Their centres are at a distance $d$ apart. The minimum speed with which a body of mass $m$ should be projected from a distance $\left(\frac{2 d}{3}\right)$ from the centre of $M_1$ so as to escape to $\propto$ is
67296.sol:
If the mass $m$ is at a distance $\frac{2}{3} d$ from the centre of $M_1$ then it is located at a distance $\frac{d}{3}$ from the centre of $M_2$.
To calculate the kinetic energy required to make the body escape Earth and moon system:
the change in gravitational potential energy between final and initial location should be equal to the kinetic energy given to the mass $m$.
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{1}{2} m v_e^2=\left[\frac{G M_1 m}{\left(\frac{2 d}{3}\right)}+\frac{G M_2 m}{\left(\frac{d}{3}\right)}\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} m v_e^2=\frac{3 G\left(M_1+2 M_2\right) m}{2 d}\end{aligned}$
Therefore, escape velocity
$v_e=\sqrt{\frac{3 G\left(M_1+2 M_2\right)}{d}}$

68088.subject: Physics
68088.text: A small metal sphere is falling through a viscous liquid. The variation of velocity ($V$) with time ($t$) is shown correctly in graph
68088.sol:
When a small metal sphere falls through a viscous liquid, the forces acting on it are its weight ($W$) downwards, buoyant force ($F_B$) upwards, and viscous drag force ($F_v$) upwards.

The equation of motion is given by:
$m \dfrac{dv}{dt} = W - F_B - F_v$
$m \dfrac{dv}{dt} = mg - \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \sigma g - 6\pi \eta r v$

Initially at $t=0$, $v=0$, so the acceleration is maximum. As velocity increases, the viscous drag force ($6\pi \eta r v$) increases, which decreases the net force and hence the acceleration.

Eventually, the net force becomes zero, and the sphere attains a constant maximum velocity called the terminal velocity ($v_T$).

The velocity varies with time according to the relation:
$v = v_T(1 - e^{-kt/m})$

This represents an exponentially increasing curve that starts from the origin and asymptotically approaches a constant value. Graph (d) correctly represents this variation.

Answer: d

68102.text: A piston of cross-sectional area $2.5 \times 10^{-2}\ \text{m}^2$ is used in a hydraulic lift to exert a force of $250\ \text{N}$ on water. The cross-sectional area of the other piston which supports a car of mass $3000\ \text{kg}$ is ($g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$)
68102.sol:
Using Pascal's law, the pressure applied on the first piston is equal to the pressure on the second piston.

$\dfrac{F_1}{A_1} = \dfrac{F_2}{A_2}$

Given $F_1 = 250\ \text{N}$, $A_1 = 2.5 \times 10^{-2}\ \text{m}^2$, $m = 3000\ \text{kg}$, and $g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$.

The force on the second piston is $F_2 = mg = 3000 \times 9.8 = 29400\ \text{N}$.

Substituting the values:

$\dfrac{250}{2.5 \times 10^{-2}} = \dfrac{29400}{A_2}$

$10000 = \dfrac{29400}{A_2}$

$A_2 = \dfrac{29400}{10000} = 2.94\ \text{m}^2$

Answer: $2.94\ \text{m}^2$

68174.text: Pure water rises through a height $h$ in a capillary tube of internal radius $r$. Surface tension of water is $T$. The pressure difference between the water level in the container and the lowest point of the concave meniscus is
68174.sol:
The pressure difference responsible for capillary rise arises from Laplace's law governing curved liquid surfaces, where the excess pressure across a spherical meniscus is given by $\Delta P = \frac{2T}{R}$, with $T$ representing surface tension and $R$ the radius of curvature.

For pure water and glass, the contact angle is approximately $0^{{}^{\circ}}$, making the meniscus hemispherical such that its radius of curvature equals the capillary's internal radius: $R = r$.

This implies the pressure difference between the water level in the container (at atmospheric pressure) and the lowest point of the concave meniscus is $\Delta P = \frac{2T}{r}$.

Among the options, C corresponds to this result: $\frac{2T}{r}$.

70044.sol:
At constant pressure, work done is:
$\begin{aligned} & \int_0^W d W=p \int_{V_1}^{V_2} d V \\ & \Rightarrow W=p\left(V_2-V_1\right)\end{aligned}$
Using, $p V=n R TW=n R\left(T_2-T_1\right)=n R \Delta T$
Now, at constant volume, heat supplied is change in internal energy:
$\begin{aligned} & d Q=n C_v \Delta T \\ & \Rightarrow \int_0^Q d Q=\int_{T_1}^{T_2} n\left(\frac{R}{\gamma-1}\right) d T \\ & \Rightarrow Q=\frac{n R\left(T_2-T_1\right)}{\left(\frac{5}{3}-1\right)}=\frac{3}{2}(n R \Delta T)=\frac{3 W}{2} \\ & Q=\frac{n R T}{\gamma-1}, \gamma=\frac{5}{3} \\ & \therefore Q=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) n R T\end{aligned}$

70410.text: In a resonance tube open at one end, the end correction is $1.1$ cm. If the shortest length of resonating air column with a tuning fork is $18$ cm, the next resonating length will be
70410.sol:
For a resonance tube closed at one end, the resonating lengths $l_1, l_2, l_3, \dots$ are related to the wavelength $\lambda$ and end correction $e$ by:

$l_1 + e = \dfrac{\lambda}{4}$

$l_2 + e = \dfrac{3\lambda}{4}$

Given $l_1 = 18$ cm and $e = 1.1$ cm.

$\dfrac{\lambda}{4} = 18 + 1.1 = 19.1$ cm

For the next resonating length $l_2$:

$l_2 + e = 3 \left( \dfrac{\lambda}{4} \right)

$l_2 + 1.1 = 3 $\times19.1$

$l_2 + 1.1 = 57.3$

$l_2 = 57.3 - 1.1 = 56.2$ cm

Answer: $56.2$ cm

71019.subject: Biology
71019.text: Which of the following does NOT occur during inspiration ?
options: Ribs and sternum move upward and outward.
Increase in pressure of thorax and the lungs.
71019.sol:
During inspiration, the diaphragm contracts and becomes flat, increasing the volume of the thoracic cavity in the antero-posterior axis.

The external intercostal muscles contract, lifting the ribs and sternum upward and outward, which increases the volume of the thoracic cavity in the dorso-ventral axis.

The overall increase in thoracic volume leads to an increase in pulmonary volume.

According to Boyle's law, an increase in volume results in a decrease in pressure. Thus, the intra-pulmonary pressure decreases below atmospheric pressure, causing air to rush into the lungs.

An increase in the pressure of the thorax and lungs occurs during expiration, not inspiration.

Answer: Increase in pressure of thorax and the lungs.

71432.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): $\text{NADH}_2$ ($\text{NADH}+\text{H}^+$) and $\text{FADH}_2$ that are produced during glycolysis, connecting link reaction and Krebs cycle, are oxidised with the help of various electron carriers and enzymes.
Statement (II): These carriers and enzymes are arranged in the cytoplasm in the form of various complexes as complex I, II, III, VI and V.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are true.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are false.
Statement (I) is true but Statement (II) is false.
Statement (I) is false but Statement (II) is true.
71432.sol:
Statement (I) is true because $\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+$ and $\text{FADH}_2$ produced during glycolysis, the link reaction, and the Krebs cycle are oxidised by the electron transport system (ETS) which consists of various electron carriers and enzymes.

Statement (II) is false because the electron carriers and enzymes of the ETS are located in the inner mitochondrial membrane, not in the cytoplasm. Furthermore, they are arranged in the form of complexes I, II, III, IV, and V, not VI.

Answer: Statement (I) is true but Statement (II) is false.

72348.text: What is the total optical path length of two media in contact with thicknesses of $d$ and $\dfrac{d}{4}$ and refractive indices of $n_1$ and $n_2$, respectively?
72348.sol:
Optical path length is given by the product of the refractive index and the geometric thickness of the medium.

For the first medium, the optical path length is $x_1 = n_1 d$.

For the second medium, the optical path length is $x_2 = n_2 \left(\dfrac{d}{4}\right).

The total optical path length is the sum of the individual optical path lengths:

$x = x_1 + x_2$

$x = n_1 d + $\dfrac{n_2 d}{4}

$ x = $\dfrac{d(4n_1 + n_2)}{4}

Answer: \dfrac{d(4n_1 + n_2)}{4}$

72423.subject: Physics
72423.text: A mono-atomic ideal gas, initially at temperature $T_1$ is enclosed in a cylinder fitted with a frictionless piston. The gas is allowed to expand adiabatically to a temperature $T_2$ by releasing the piston suddenly. $L_1 and L_2$ are the lengths of gas columns before and after the expansion, respectively. The value of $\dfrac{T_1}{T_2}$ is $\left[\gamma=\dfrac{5}{3}\right]$
72423.sol:
For a reversible adiabatic process, the relationship between temperature and volume is given by $TV^{\gamma - 1} = \text{constant}$.

Applying this to the initial and final states of the gas:

$T_1 V_1^{\gamma - 1} = T_2 V_2^{\gamma - 1}$

$\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right)^{\gamma - 1}$

Let $A$ be the cross-sectional area of the cylinder. The volume of the gas column of length $L$ is $V = AL$.

Substituting $V_1 = AL_1$ and $V_2 = AL_2$:

$\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \left(\dfrac{AL_2}{AL_1}\right)^{\gamma - 1} = \left(\dfrac{L_2}{L_1}\right)^{\gamma - 1}$

Given that the gas is mono-atomic, $\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

$\gamma - 1 = \dfrac{5}{3} - 1 = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Substituting this value into the equation:

$\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \left(\dfrac{L_2}{L_1}\right)^{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{L_2}{L_1}\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}$

The magnetic field lines inside a long straight solenoid carrying current are in the form of parallel straight lines. This indicates that the magnetic field is the same at all points inside the solenoid.

The magnitude of the magnetic field inside an ideal long solenoid is given by $B = \mu_0 n I$, where $n$ is the number of turns per unit length and $I$ is the current. Since $\mu_0$, $n$, and $I$ are constant, the magnetic field is uniform inside the solenoid.

75165.subject: General Ability
75165.text:
Condensation of water vapour into water is influenced by which of the following factor/factors?
1. Volume of air
2. Humidity
3. Temperature

Select the answer using the code given below:
75165.sol:
Condensation is the process of transformation of water vapour into liquid water, which is primarily caused by the loss of heat.

Condensation depends upon the amount of cooling and the relative humidity of the air. It is influenced by the volume of air, temperature, pressure, and humidity.

Condensation takes place under the following conditions:
1. When the temperature of the air is reduced to the dew point with its volume remaining constant.
2. When both the volume and the temperature are reduced.
3. When moisture is added to the air through evaporation.

Thus, volume of air, humidity, and temperature all influence the condensation of water vapour.

Answer: 1, 2 and 3

83494.subject: Physics
83494.text:
Two statements are given below :
A. When the forward bias voltage across a p-n junction diode increases above a certain threshold voltage, the diode current increases significantly.
B. This current is called reverse saturation current.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statements A and B are true
Statement A is true, but Statement B is false
Both Statements A and B are false
Statement A is false, but Statement B is true
83494.sol:
Statement A describes the behavior of a p-n junction diode under forward bias. When the applied voltage exceeds the threshold voltage (or cut-in voltage), the potential barrier is overcome, and the forward current increases exponentially. Thus, Statement A is true.

Statement B claims this current is the reverse saturation current. This is incorrect because the current flowing under forward bias is the forward current. Reverse saturation current is a very small current that flows under reverse bias conditions due to minority charge carriers. Thus, Statement B is false.

Therefore, Statement A is true, but Statement B is false.

Answer: Statement A is true, but Statement B is false

96261.text:
Meiosis and mitosis are found to be the two types of cell division. A cell is observed to have 50 chromosomes in its nucleus during interphase before entering S-phase. How many chromosomes will it have after undergoing division by the two-division process?
&
& Meiosis Mitosis
$1$ $100$ $25$
$2$ $50$ $50$
$3$ $50$ $100$
$4$ $25$ $50$
96261.sol: Meiosis is a type of reductional division process where the chromosome number is halved in the daughter cell compared to its parent cell. It is significant in the process of reproduction for making gametes. Mitosis is a type of cell division where the chromosome number between parent cell and daughter cell remains the same. It is also called as equational division. Therefore, if parent cell has 50 chromosomes then after mitosis the daughter cell will have 50 chromosomes as well but after meiosis, the daughter cell formed will have 25 chromosomes only. Thus, row 4th is the correct answer.

96413.subject: Botany
96413.text:
Identify the correct sequence of steps involved in the process of decomposition.

(a) Humification

(b)& Catabolism

(c) Fragmentation of detritus

(d) Leaching

(e)& Mineralization
96413.sol:
Decomposition is a process in which the physical and chemical breakdown of complex organic matter will take place& with the help of decomposers. The& basic steps involve-

Fragmentation of detritus – Leaching – Catabolism – Humification – Mineralization.

A) & Fragmentation of Detritus: Small invertebrate animals called detritivores or detritophages feed on detritus, e.g., earthworms, termites they bring about its fragmentation.
B) Leaching: Part of water-soluble substances present in the fragmented and decomposition detritus (e.g., sugars, inorganic nutrients) go down into the soil horizon by percolating water and get precipitated as unavailable salts.

C) Catabolism: It is carried out by saprotrophic bacteria and fungi. They secrete digestive enzymes over the fragmented detritus. The enzymes degrade complex organic compounds into simple inorganic substances.
D) Humification. It is the process of decomposition of detritus to form humus. Humus is a dark-coloured, amorphous, more or less decomposed organic matter rich in cellulose, lignin, tannins, resin, etc. and is highly resistant against microbial action. It undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate. Humus is slightly acidic, colloidal, and functions as a reservoir of nutrients.

E) Mineralization. It is the release of inorganic substances by saprophytic microbes (e.g.. CO_{2}, H_{2}O, minerals) from organic matter or humus during the process of decomposition. They are formed along with simple and soluble organic substances when digestive enzymes are poured over organic matter by saprotrophic microbes.

97359.text: The most delicate stage in the life cycle of an angiosperm where maximum mortality observed is the
97359.sol: Seed germination is the process where seed develops into a new plant by producing the shoot and root on germination. The germinated seed forms a young sporophyte called a seedling. 102462.subject: Physics
102462.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When two different masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ ($m_1 > m_2$) attached to identical springs oscillate with the same amplitude, the lighter mass $m_2$ will possess a greater maximum kinetic energy.

Reason (R): The maximum kinetic energy of a spring-mass system depends only on the spring constant and the amplitude, and is independent of the mass.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
102462.sol:
The maximum kinetic energy of a spring-mass system is given by $K_{\max} = \dfrac{1}{2} m v_{\max}^2$.

Since $v_{\max} = A\omega$ and $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$, substituting these gives:
$K_{\max} = \dfrac{1}{2} m \left(A \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} k A^2$.

This shows that the maximum kinetic energy depends only on the spring constant $k$ and the amplitude $A$. It is completely independent of the mass $m$. Therefore, the Reason (R) is correct.

Because both masses are attached to identical springs (same $k$) and oscillate with the same amplitude (same $A$), they will have exactly the same maximum kinetic energy. The lighter mass will have a higher maximum velocity, but its smaller mass exactly compensates for this, keeping the maximum kinetic energy constant. Therefore, the Assertion (A) is not correct.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

104100.subject: Physics
104100.text: In a series LCR circuit, the impedance is $10\ \Omega$ and the rms current flowing through it is $5\text{ A}$. The rms voltages across the resistor and the inductor are $30\text{ V}$ and $50\text{ V}$, respectively. If the voltage across the capacitor is greater than the voltage across the inductor, the rms voltage across the capacitor is:
104100.sol:
The rms voltage of the source is given by Ohm's law for the entire circuit:

$V_{\text{rms}} = Z \times I_{\text{rms}} = 10 \times 5 = 50\text{ V}$

Using the phasor addition formula for voltages in a series LCR circuit:

$V_{\text{rms}}^2 = V_R^2 + (V_C - V_L)^2$

Substituting the known values:

$50^2 = 30^2 + (V_C - 50)^2$

$2500 = 900 + (V_C - 50)^2$

$(V_C - 50)^2 = 1600$

Taking the square root on both sides:

$V_C - 50 = \pm 40$

This gives two possible values for $V_C$:
$V_C = 50 + 40 = 90\text{ V}$
or
$V_C = 50 - 40 = 10\text{ V}$

Since it is given that the voltage across the capacitor is greater than the voltage across the inductor ($V_C > V_L$, i.e., $V_C > 50\text{ V}$), we select $V_C = 90\text{ V}$.

Answer: $90\text{ V}$

104145.subject: Physics
104145.text: An alternating current given by $I = I_0 \sin \omega t$ flows through a purely inductive circuit of inductance $L$. Which of the following expressions represents the instantaneous power $P$ supplied to the inductor by the source?
104145.sol:
The voltage across a pure inductor is given by $V = L \dfrac{dI}{dt}$.

Given $I = I_0 \sin \omega t$, we have:
$V = L \dfrac{d}{dt}(I_0 \sin \omega t) = \omega L I_0 \cos \omega t$

The instantaneous power $P$ is the product of instantaneous voltage and current:
$P = V \times I = (\omega L I_0 \cos \omega t)(I_0 \sin \omega t)$

Using the trigonometric identity $2 \sin \theta \cos \theta = \sin 2\theta$, we get:
$P = \dfrac{1}{2} \omega L I_0^2 (2 \sin \omega t \cos \omega t) = \dfrac{1}{2} \omega L I_0^2 \sin 2\omega t$

Note that while the average power over a complete cycle is zero, the instantaneous power varies sinusoidally with twice the frequency of the source.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2} \omega L I_0^2 \sin 2\omega t$

104499.subject: Physics
104499.text: A converging beam of light is directed towards a point P. A concave lens of focal length $15$ cm is placed in the path of the beam such that point P is $10$ cm behind the concave lens. A convex lens of focal length $20$ cm is placed $10$ cm behind the concave lens. The final image formed by the combination is located at:
options: $80$ cm in front of the convex lens
104499.sol:
For the first lens (concave lens):
The converging beam is directed towards point P, which acts as a virtual object.
Object distance, $u_1 = +10$ cm
Focal length, $f_1 = -15$ cm
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{-15}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30}$
$\Rightarrow v_1 = +30$ cm
The intermediate image is formed $30$ cm behind the concave lens. This acts as a virtual object for the second lens.

For the second lens (convex lens):
Distance between the lenses, $d = 10$ cm
Object distance for the convex lens, $u_2 = v_1 - d = 30 - 10 = +20$ cm (virtual object)
Focal length, $f_2 = +20$ cm
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{2}{20} = \dfrac{1}{10}$
$\Rightarrow v_2 = +10$ cm

The positive sign indicates that the final image is formed $10$ cm behind (to the right of) the convex lens.

Answer: $10$ cm behind the convex lens

104702.subject: Physics
104702.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Two independent monochromatic light bulbs emitting light of the exact same wavelength can be used to produce a sustained interference pattern on a screen.
Reason (R): The phase difference between the light waves emitted by two independent sources changes randomly and rapidly with time.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
104702.sol:
Assertion (A) is false. For a sustained interference pattern to be formed, the two sources of light must be coherent, meaning they must emit light waves with a constant phase difference. Two independent light bulbs, even if they emit light of the exact same wavelength, are incoherent sources and cannot produce a sustained interference pattern.

Reason (R) is true. In independent light sources, light is emitted by millions of atoms undergoing transitions randomly. As a result, the phase of the emitted light changes abruptly and randomly. Therefore, the phase difference between the waves from two independent sources changes rapidly with time, averaging the interference term to zero over any macroscopic time interval.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

107025.text: The correct increasing order of atomic radii of the elements $\mathrm{Li}, \mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{K}$ and $\mathrm{Rb}$ is
107025.sol:
As we move down a group in the periodic table, the principal quantum number increases and new electron shells are added. This effect outweighs the increase in nuclear charge, causing the atomic radius to increase down the group.

The given elements belong to Group 1 (alkali metals) and their order from top to bottom is $\mathrm{Li}, \mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{K}, \mathrm{Rb}$.

Therefore, the correct increasing order of their atomic radii is $\mathrm{Li} \lt \mathrm{Na} \lt \mathrm{K} \lt \mathrm{Rb}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{Li} \lt \mathrm{Na} \lt \mathrm{K} \lt \mathrm{Rb}$

109375.subject: Chemistry
109375.text: Which of the following mixtures will result in a buffer solution with maximum buffer capacity?
options: $30\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M HCOOH} + 30\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M KOH}$
$20\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M HCOOH} + 40\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M KOH}$
$40\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M HCOOH} + 20\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M KOH}$
$50\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M HCOOH} + 10\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M KOH}$
109375.sol:
A buffer solution has maximum buffer capacity when the concentration of the weak acid equals the concentration of its conjugate base (i.e., $\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a$). This requires neutralizing exactly half of the weak acid.

Let us calculate the millimoles (mmol) for the mixture in option 3:
Initial mmol of $\text{HCOOH} = 40\text{ mL} \times 0.2\text{ M} = 8\text{ mmol}$
Initial mmol of $\text{KOH} = 20\text{ mL} \times 0.2\text{ M} = 4\text{ mmol}$

The neutralization reaction is:
$\text{HCOOH} + \text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{HCOOK} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Since $\text{KOH}$ is the limiting reagent, $4\text{ mmol}$ of $\text{KOH}$ will react with $4\text{ mmol}$ of $\text{HCOOH}$ to form $4\text{ mmol}$ of $\text{HCOOK}$.
Remaining $\text{HCOOH} = 8 - 4 = 4\text{ mmol}$.

The final solution contains $4\text{ mmol}$ of $\text{HCOOH}$ and $4\text{ mmol}$ of $\text{HCOOK}$. Since $[\text{Weak Acid}] = [\text{Salt}]$, the buffer has maximum capacity.

In contrast:
Option 1 forms only salt (complete neutralization).
Option 2 leaves excess strong base (not a buffer).
Option 4 leaves $8\text{ mmol}$ acid and $2\text{ mmol}$ salt (ratio $4:1$, not maximum capacity).

Answer: $40\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M HCOOH} + 20\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M KOH}$

113928.subject: Chemistry
113928.text: When chloroform and acetone are mixed, they form a non-ideal solution. Which of the following correctly describes the type of deviation from Raoult's law and the thermodynamic properties of this mixture?
113928.sol:
When chloroform and acetone are mixed, a hydrogen bond is formed between the highly polarized carbon-hydrogen bond of chloroform and the oxygen atom of acetone.

This makes the intermolecular (A-B) interactions stronger than the pure component (A-A and B-B) interactions. Consequently, the escaping tendency of molecules decreases, leading to a negative deviation from Raoult's law.

For solutions showing negative deviation, the stronger interactions lead to a release of energy ($\Delta_{\text{mix}}H < 0$) and a decrease in volume upon mixing ($\Delta_{\text{mix}}V < 0$).

Answer: Negative deviation, $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H < 0$, $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V < 0$

114923.subject: Chemistry
114923.text: For a reaction $X \rightarrow Y$, the plot of reactant concentration $[X]$ versus time is a straight line with a slope of $-4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ M s}^{-1}$. If the initial concentration of $X$ is $0.24 \text{ M}$, what is the half-life of the reaction?
114923.sol:
The plot of reactant concentration $[X]$ versus time is a straight line, which indicates that the reaction follows zero-order kinetics.

For a zero-order reaction, the integrated rate equation is $[X] = -kt + [X]_0$.

Comparing this with the equation of a straight line $y = mx + c$, the slope $m = -k$.

Given slope $= -4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ M s}^{-1}$, so the rate constant $k = 4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ M s}^{-1}$.

The half-life for a zero-order reaction is given by $t_{1/2} = \dfrac{[X]_0}{2k}$.

Substituting the given values:
$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.24}{2 \times 4 \times 10^{-3}} = \dfrac{0.24}{0.008} = 30 \text{ s}$.

Answer: $30 \text{ s}$

116362.subject: Chemistry
116362.text: What is the number of moles of ammonia produced when $56\text{ g}$ of nitrogen gas reacts completely with excess hydrogen gas in Haber's process?
116362.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for Haber's process is:

$\text{N}_{2}(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_{2}(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_{3}(\text{g})$

First, calculate the number of moles of nitrogen gas ($\text{N}_{2}$):
Molar mass of $\text{N}_{2} = 28\text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Moles of $\text{N}_{2} = \dfrac{56\text{ g}}{28\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 2\text{ moles}$

According to the stoichiometry of the reaction, $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{N}_{2}$ produces $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{NH}_{3}$.
Therefore, $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{N}_{2}$ will produce $2 \times 2 = 4\text{ moles}$ of $\text{NH}_{3}$.

Answer: $4$

117783.subject: Chemistry
117783.text: Which of the following pairs of coordination compounds has the same value of spin-only magnetic moment?
117783.sol:
In $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$, Co is in +3 oxidation state ($3\text{d}^{6}$). $\text{F}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so it forms a high spin complex with configuration $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{4} \text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}$. Number of unpaired electrons ($n$) = 4.

In $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$, Fe is in +2 oxidation state ($3\text{d}^{6}$). $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ is a weak field ligand, so it forms a high spin complex with configuration $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{4} \text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}$. Number of unpaired electrons ($n$) = 4.

Since both have $n=4$, their spin-only magnetic moment is $\sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} = 4.90 \text{ BM}$.

For other options:
$\left[\text{Mn}(\text{CN})_{6}\right]^{3-}$: $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ ($3\text{d}^{4}$), strong field ligand $\rightarrow$ $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{4} \text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}$ ($n=2$).
$\left[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_{6}\right]^{3-}$: $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ($3\text{d}^{5}$), strong field ligand $\rightarrow$ $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{5} \text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}$ ($n=1$).
$\left[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_{4}\right]$: $\text{Ni}^{0}$ ($3\text{d}^{10}$), $n=0$.
$\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$: $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($3\text{d}^{8}$), weak field ligand $\rightarrow$ $n=2$.
$\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$: $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ($3\text{d}^{6}$), strong field ligand $\rightarrow$ $n=0$.
$\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$: $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($3\text{d}^{3}$), $n=3$.

Answer: $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ and $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$

119883.subject: Chemistry
119883.text: Compound $\mathrm{A}$ having molecular formula $\mathrm{C_3H_7NO}$ is treated with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ in the presence of aqueous $\mathrm{KOH}$ to give compound $\mathrm{B}$. Compound $\mathrm{B}$ is further heated with chloroform and alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$ to produce compound $\mathrm{C}$. The compound $\mathrm{C}$ is :
119883.sol:
Compound $\mathrm{A}$ with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_3H_7NO}$ is propanamide ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CONH_2}$).

When propanamide is treated with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ and aqueous $\mathrm{KOH}$, it undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation. This is a step-down reaction where the carbonyl carbon is lost, yielding ethanamine ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$) as compound $\mathrm{B}$.

Heating a primary amine like ethanamine with chloroform ($\mathrm{CHCl_3}$) and alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$ results in the Carbylamine reaction. This produces an isocyanide with a highly unpleasant odour. Thus, ethanamine is converted to ethyl isocyanide ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NC}$) as compound $\mathrm{C}$.

Propyl isocyanide and propyl cyanide are incorrect because they do not account for the loss of one carbon atom during the Hoffmann bromamide degradation. Ethyl cyanide is incorrect because the Carbylamine reaction yields an isocyanide, not a cyanide.

Answer: Ethyl isocyanide

121699.subject: Botany
121699.text: In which algae does isogamous reproduction with non-flagellated gametes occur?
121699.sol: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These <mark>gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra).</mark> Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus

121735.subject: Botany
121735.text: What does the protoplast of brown algae contain?
options: A centrally located vacuole, nucleus, and plastids
121735.sol: The members of phaeophyceae or brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats. They show great variation in size and form. They range from simple branched, filamentous forms (Ectocarpus) to profusely branched forms as represented by kelps, which may reach a height of 100 meters. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. They vary in color from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them. Food is stored as complex carbohydrates, which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol. The vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin. <mark>The protoplast contains, in addition to plastids, a centrally located vacuole and nucleus</mark>. The plant body is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and has a stalk, the stipe and leaf-like photosynthetic organ – the frond. Vegetative reproduction takes place by fragmentation. Asexual reproduction in most brown algae is by biflagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped and have two unequal laterally attached flagella.

123484.sol:
Due to continued formation of secondary tissues in the older stem and roots however the epidermis gets stressed and ultimately tends to rupture and followed by death of epidermal cells and outer tissues, and a new protective layer is developed called periderm. Structurally it consists of three parts Phellogen or Cork cambium, phellem or cork and phelloderm.
Usually in the periderm of most plants, certain areas with loosely arranged cells have been found, which possess more or less raised and corky spots where the underneath tissues break through the epidermis. 123556.subject: Botany
123556.text: How long does the cell division proper last in the 24 hour average duration of cell cycle of a human cell?
123556.sol: The M Phase represents the phase when the actual cell division or mitosis occurs and the interphase represents the phase between two successive M phases. It is significant to note that in the 24 hour average duration of cell cycle of a human cell, cell division proper lasts for only about an hour. The interphase lasts more than 95% of the duration of cell cycle. The M Phase starts with the nuclear division, corresponding to the separation of daughter chromosomes (karyokinesis) and usually ends with division of cytoplasm (cytokinesis).

123570.subject: Botany
123570.text: Which cells in adult animals do not exhibit division?
123570.sol: Some cells in the adult animals do not appear to exhibit division (e.g.,heart cells) and many other cells divide only occasionally, as needed to replace cells that have been lost because of injury or cell death. These cells that do not divide further exit G1 phase to enter an inactive stage called quiescent stage (G0) of the cell cycle. Cells in this stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism. In animals, mitotic cell division is only seen in the diploid somatic cells.

123668.sol: This is followed by the second stage of prophase I called zygotene. During this stage chromosomes start pairing together and this process of association is called synapsis. Such paired chromosomes are called homologous chromosomes. Crossing over is also an enzyme-mediated process and the enzyme involved is called recombinase. Crossing over leads to recombination of genetic material on the two chromosomes. Recombination between homologous chromosomes is completed by the end of pachytene, leaving the chromosomes linked at the sites of crossing over.

123818.subject: Botany
123818.text: During meiosis I, the complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent. In which stage of prophase I do the four chromatids of each bivalent become distinct and clearly appear as tetrads?
123818.sol:
According to NCERT, during the zygotene stage, homologous chromosomes start pairing together to form bivalents. However, these bivalents are not clearly visible at this stage.

The first two stages of prophase I (leptotene and zygotene) are relatively short-lived compared to the next stage, which is pachytene. During the pachytene stage, the four chromatids of each bivalent chromosome become distinct and clearly appear as tetrads. Students often confuse the formation of bivalents (zygotene) with their clear visibility as tetrads (pachytene).

Answer: Pachytene

125168.text:
Read the following statements carefully:
A. Glycolysis is also known as the EMP pathway and is the only process in respiration for anaerobic organisms.
B. The enzyme pyruvate dehydrogenase requires $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ for the oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate.
C. The TCA cycle starts with the condensation of an acetyl group with citric acid to yield oxaloacetic acid.
D. The formation of ATP through the electron transport system in mitochondria is called oxidative phosphorylation.

How many of the above statements are correct?
125168.sol:
Statement A is correct: The scheme of glycolysis was given by Embden, Meyerhof, and Parnas (EMP pathway) and it is the only respiration process in anaerobic organisms.

Statement B is correct: The oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA is catalysed by pyruvate dehydrogenase, which requires $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ along with $\text{NAD}^{+}$ and CoA.

Statement C is incorrect: The TCA cycle starts with the condensation of an acetyl group with oxaloacetic acid (OAA) and water to yield citric acid, not the reverse.

Statement D is correct: The synthesis of ATP using the energy of oxidation-reduction in the mitochondria is called oxidative phosphorylation.

Therefore, exactly three statements (A, B, and D) are correct.

Answer: Three

125342.subject: Botany
125342.text: What is the color of chlorophyll b in the chromatogram?
125342.sol: Looking at plants have you ever wondered why and how there are so many shades of green in their leaves – even in the same plant? We can look for an answer to this question by trying to separate the leaf pigments of any green plant through paper chromatography. A chromatographic separation of the leaf pigments shows that the colour that we see in leaves is not due to a single pigment but due to four pigments: Chlorophyll a (bright or blue green in the chromatogram), chlorophyll b (yellow green), xanthophylls (yellow) and carotenoids (yellow to yellow-orange). Let us now see what roles various pigments play in photosynthesis.

125383.sol: When only PS I is functional, the electron is circulated within the photosystem and the phosphorylation occurs due to cyclic flow of electrons. A possible location where this could be happening is in the stroma lamellae. While the membrane or lamellae of the grana have both PS I and PS II the stroma lamellae membranes lack PS II as well as NADP reductase enzyme. The excited electron does not pass on to NADP+ but is cycled back to the PS I complex through the electron transport chain. The cyclic flow hence, results only in the synthesis of ATP, but not of NADPH + H+ . Cyclic photophosphorylation also occurs when only light of wavelengths beyond 680 nm are available for excitation.

127570.subject: Botany
127570.text: What is the primary production in an ecosystem?
options: The rate of organic matter production in photosynthesis
The rate of new organic matter formation by consumers
The amount of energy produced by plants
127570.sol: A constant input of solar energy is the basic requirement for any ecosystem to function and sustain. Primary production is defined as the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. It is expressed in terms of weight (g m–2) or energy (kcal m–2). The rate of biomass production is called productivity. It is expressed in terms of gm–2 yr –1 or (kcal m–2) yr–1 to compare the productivity of different ecosystems. It can be divided into gross primary productivity (GPP) and net primary productivity (NPP). Gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by plants in respiration. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R), is the net primary productivity (NPP). GPP – R = NPP Net primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbiviores and decomposers). Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers. Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. It also depends on a variety of environmental factors, availability of nutrients and photosynthetic capacity of plants. Therefore, it varies in different types of ecosystems. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Of this, despite occupying about 70 per cent of the surface, the productivity of the oceans are only 55 billion tons. Rest of course, is on land. Discuss the main reason for the low productivity of ocean with your teacher.
